PANCE Histology & Microscopy Findings 
Buzzword findings that appear in PANCE clinical vignettes (grouped by organ system) 
Note:   Histology is not a formal PANCE task category. The 2025 NCCPA blueprint tests pathophysiology under   Applying Foundational Scientific Concepts (8%) , with the skill of   relating pathophysiologic principles to
specific disease processes . Microscopy/biopsy/cytology results appear inside clinical vignettes - this chart covers the high-yield buzzwords PA prep resources consistently emphasize. 
Finding   Associated Disease   Why It Matters Clinically
HEMATOLOGIC / LYMPHOID 
Reed-Sternberg cells   Hodgkin lymphoma   Bimodal age distribution; staging with PET-CT; curative-intent ABVD chemo 
Auer rods   Acute myeloid leukemia (AML)   If APL/M3 with t(15;17): treat with ATRA + arsenic (DIC risk before treatment) 
Smudge cells (peripheral smear)   Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)   Often incidental on routine CBC in older adults 
Howell-Jolly bodies   Asplenia / post-splenectomy   Mandates pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib vaccination 
Heinz bodies / bite cells   G6PD deficiency hemolysis   Avoid sulfa drugs, fava beans, primaquine, dapsone 
Hypersegmented neutrophils   B12 / folate deficiency (megaloblastic anemia)   Distinguishes megaloblastic from iron-deficiency microcytic anemia 
Schistocytes (helmet cells, fragments)   MAHA - TTP, HUS, DIC, HELLP   TTP pentad = emergency; plasma exchange; do NOT transfuse platelets in TTP 
Spherocytes   Hereditary spherocytosis OR warm autoimmune
hemolytic anemia
Direct Coombs:   positive   = AIHA;   negative   = HS (osmotic fragility +) 
Sickle cells / target cells / Howell-Jolly   Sickle cell disease   Confirm with Hgb electrophoresis; vaso-occlusive crisis = pain + hydration + opioids 
Tear-drop cells (dacrocytes)   Myelofibrosis (or other marrow infiltration)   Often with leukoerythroblastic smear and dry tap on bone marrow aspirate 
Rouleaux formation   Multiple myeloma   Pair with M-spike on SPEP, hypercalcemia, lytic bone lesions, renal failure 
Basophilic stippling   Lead poisoning, sideroblastic anemia, thalassemia   Lead in children   →   chelation; check Pb, FEP/ZPP 
Target cells   Thalassemia, HbC, liver disease, asplenia   Helps narrow microcytic anemia differential 
MSK / JOINT ASPIRATE (POLARIZED MICROSCOPY) 
Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals
(yellow parallel) 
Gout (monosodium urate)   Acute: NSAIDs, colchicine, or steroids. Chronic: allopurinol/febuxostat (NOT during flare) 
Rhomboid, positively birefringent crystals (blue
parallel) 
Pseudogout (CPPD)   Knees most common; chondrocalcinosis on X-ray; NSAIDs/colchicine/steroids 
Apple-green birefringence on Congo red stain   Amyloidosis (AL, AA)   Suspect with nephrotic syndrome + restrictive cardiomyopathy + neuropathy 
PULMONARY 
Non-caseating granulomas   Sarcoidosis   African-American adult, bilateral hilar adenopathy; ACE may be elevated; treat with steroids if symptomatic 
Caseating granulomas (Ghon focus / complex)   Tuberculosis   RIPE therapy (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) + contact tracing 
Ferruginous bodies   Asbestosis   Pleural plaques on CXR;   ↑   risk of mesothelioma and bronchogenic carcinoma 
Curschmann spirals / Charcot-Leyden crystals   Asthma (sputum)   Eosinophilic inflammation; supports asthma over COPD when smoker is unclear 
ENDOCRINE 
Orphan-Annie eye nuclei + psammoma bodies   Papillary thyroid carcinoma   Best-prognosis thyroid cancer; total thyroidectomy ± radioactive iodine 
Amyloid stroma (calcitonin staining)   Medullary thyroid carcinoma   Screen for MEN2 / RET mutation; check calcitonin and CEA 
Lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal centers
(Hurthle cells) 
Hashimoto thyroiditis   Anti-TPO and anti-thyroglobulin antibodies; treat with levothyroxine 
GASTROINTESTINAL / HEPATIC

Finding   Associated Disease   Why It Matters Clinically 
Non-caseating granulomas + skip lesions (terminal
ileum) 
Crohn disease   Steroids/biologics; surgery is NOT curative (transmural, mouth-to-anus) 
Crypt abscesses, continuous mucosal inflammation   Ulcerative colitis   Limited to colon; total colectomy is curative;   ↑   risk of colon cancer 
Signet-ring cells   Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma (linitis plastica)   Aggressive; H. pylori is the major risk for the intestinal type 
RENAL / URINE SEDIMENT 
RBC casts / dysmorphic RBCs   Glomerulonephritis (nephritic syndrome)   Hematuria + HTN + edema + proteinuria; identifies glomerular bleeding 
WBC casts   Pyelonephritis or acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)   Pyelo: fever + flank pain + CVA tenderness. AIN: drug reaction (NSAIDs, PPIs, abx) 
Muddy-brown / granular casts   Acute tubular necrosis (ATN)   Most common cause of intrinsic AKI; ischemic or nephrotoxic 
Broad / waxy casts   Chronic kidney disease   Indicates chronic tubular dilation 
Fatty casts / oval fat bodies (Maltese cross)   Nephrotic syndrome   Heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia 
REPRODUCTIVE / VAGINITIS 
Koilocytes (Pap smear)   HPV-related cervical dysplasia   Triggers colposcopy per ASCCP guidelines 
Clue cells (saline wet mount)   Bacterial vaginosis   Whiff test +, pH >4.5; treat with metronidazole 
Pseudohyphae / budding yeast (KOH)   Vulvovaginal candidiasis   Treat with fluconazole 150 mg or topical azole 
Motile trichomonads (saline)   Trichomoniasis (STI)   Strawberry cervix; treat patient AND partner with metronidazole 
INFECTIOUS DISEASE 
Owl's-eye intranuclear inclusions   Cytomegalovirus (CMV)   Especially in HIV (CD4 <50: retinitis) and transplant; treat with ganciclovir 
Multinucleated giant cells (Tzanck smear)   HSV or VZV   Distinguishes herpetic vesicles from other vesiculobullous conditions 
Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci   Streptococcus pneumoniae   Most common cause of CAP and bacterial meningitis in adults 
Acid-fast bacilli (Ziehl-Neelsen)   Mycobacterium tuberculosis (or NTM)   Confirm with NAAT/culture; report to public health 
Gram-negative diplococci (intracellular)   Neisseria gonorrhoeae   Cervical/urethral discharge; ceftriaxone + doxycycline (chlamydia coverage) 
DERMATOLOGY 
Acantholysis / tombstone basal cells (Tzanck)   Pemphigus vulgaris   IgG vs desmoglein-3; Nikolsky sign +; mortality if untreated; steroids 
Subepidermal bulla with eosinophils   Bullous pemphigoid   IgG vs hemidesmosomes; tense bullae; Nikolsky negative; better prognosis than PV 
Munro microabscesses (parakeratosis, no granular
layer) 
Psoriasis   Usually clinical dx; biopsy if uncertain; treat with topical steroids, vit D analogs, phototherapy, biologics 
NEURO 
Lewy bodies ( α -synuclein inclusions)   Parkinson disease / Dementia with Lewy bodies   DLB triad: fluctuating cognition, visual hallucinations, parkinsonism. AVOID typical antipsychotics
